items.followUp: A car moving at 25 m s⁻¹ slows uniformly to 10 m s⁻¹ in 3 s. Find its retardation.

rubric.why: These are the correctly identified initial velocity, final velocity and time.
rubric.description: States the given data in SI units.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly identifying all three values.

rubric.why: This equation gives acceleration from the change in velocity over time.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct formula.

rubric.why: The given velocities and time are substituted correctly.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct substitution.

rubric.description: Calculates the acceleration with its unit.

rubric.why: Retardation is the positive magnitude of the negative acceleration.
rubric.description: States the retardation with its unit.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for 3 m s⁻² as retardation.

modelAnswer: Given: u = 30 m s⁻¹, v = 15 m s⁻¹, t = 5 s.
Retardation is the magnitude of acceleration, so retardation = 3 m s⁻².

items.followUp: A force has an x-component of 8 N and a y-component of 6 N. Find its magnitude and direction relative to the positive x-axis.

rubric.why: The two perpendicular force components are correctly identified.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying both components as 12 N and 5 N.

rubric.why: The Pythagorean relation gives the magnitude of the resultant of perpendicular components.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct formula.

rubric.why: The components are correctly substituted into the magnitude formula.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct substitution.

rubric.why: The resultant force has magnitude 13 N.
The angle is measured from the positive x-axis towards the positive y-component.
rubric.description: Gives the direction of the resultant.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for approximately 22.6° above the positive x-axis or an equivalent inverse-tangent calculation with the correct direction.

modelAnswer: Given: Fx = 12 N and Fy = 5 N.
Substitution: F = sqrt(12^2 + 5^2) N = sqrt(169) N.
Direction: θ = tan^-1(Fy/Fx) = tan^-1(5/12) ≈ 22.6° above the positive x-axis.

items.followUp: What are prefixes in measurement? Give one example of a multiple and one example of a submultiple.

rubric.why: Prefixes are written before units to indicate multiples or submultiples of those units.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that prefixes written before units indicate multiples or submultiples.

rubric.why: The examples correctly pair prefixes with their powers of ten or decimal values.
rubric.description: Gives two examples of prefixes and their meanings.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for two correct prefix examples with their values.

modelAnswer: Prefixes are symbols or words written before units to indicate multiples or submultiples of the units.

items.followUp: Define acceleration due to gravity and state its approximate value on the surface of Earth.

rubric.why: Gravitational acceleration is the acceleration of a freely falling body due to gravity.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking the acceleration of a freely falling body to gravity.

rubric.why: The approximate value of gravitational acceleration at Earth's surface is 9.8 m s⁻².
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for approximately 9.8 m s⁻² or 9.81 m s⁻².

modelAnswer: Gravitational acceleration is the acceleration acquired by a freely falling body due to the gravitational force of Earth.
Its value at the surface of Earth is approximately 9.8 m s⁻².
